title: Yin Chih Wen: The Tract of the Quiet Way
altTitles: The Tract of the Quiet Way
dateDisplay: Attributed to Wenchang; widely circulated from the 17th century
attributionNote: The tract is presented as the revelation of Wenchang, the god of literature, and was widely printed by moral-instruction societies in the Qing. Its composition is anonymous and its attribution traditional.
description: The Tract of the Quiet Way is a Qing-dynasty morality book in the tradition of the Tai Shang Tractate: a list of the good deeds that heaven secretly rewards and the evils it punishes, addressed to ordinary households and offered as a guide to hidden virtue. It recommends compassion for the poor, respect for life, honesty in trade, and the quiet accumulation of merit that does not seek recognition.
historicalContext: The Yin Chih Wen circulated through the charitable and moral-instruction societies of the Qing, often printed together with the Kan Ying P'ien. Teitaro Suzuki and Paul Carus translated it, with the Chinese commentator's notes and their own, for the Open Court Publishing Company in 1906, as part of their effort to present Chinese religion to Western readers.
availabilityNote: Complete text. The tract itself is streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time and presented as one chapter; the Chinese commentator's notes, the translators' notes and the index printed with it are not part of the work.
